title: Exfiltration Over Other Network Medium: Exfiltration Over Bluetooth
shortTitle: Exfiltration Over Other Network Medium: Exfiltration Over...
summary: Exfiltration over Bluetooth is the sub-technique of using a short range radio pairing to move collected data off a host. It differs from its parent only in the medium: the transfer travels over Bluetooth instead of a wireless, cellular or modem link, and the practical consequence is proximity. Bluetooth reaches roughly room distance, so the adversary either needs hardware near the target or must first pair a device with the victim machine, and the achievable throughput is low, which pushes operators towards small, compressed payloads sent over a longer period. On the host, evidence is limited to adapter and radio state, pairing and profile records, Bluetooth service and driver activity, and endpoint telemetry showing a pairing utility or service being started. Network monitoring sees nothing, because the traffic never crosses a monitored boundary. Defenders therefore depend on host logging, wireless policy and physical awareness of what hardware is allowed near sensitive systems.

beginner.definition: Bluetooth is a short range radio link used by phones, headsets and computers. This technique means copying stolen data from a computer to a nearby device over that link. The parent technique covers any other network medium, such as wireless or mobile data. This sub-technique covers just the Bluetooth radio, so it needs the attacker or their device to be physically close.
beginner.whyItMatters: Bluetooth traffic does not pass through the company network, so network tools cannot see it. The range is short, but an attacker inside the building or a planted device is enough. Many companies switch Bluetooth on everywhere and never review the pairings. That leaves a quiet path out of the building.
howItWorks: The attacker gathers the files they want and packs them into a small archive.
A device near the target computer starts a Bluetooth pairing request with it.
If the computer accepts, the two devices can now exchange data over radio.
The archive is split into small pieces and sent across the link slowly.
A nearby phone or laptop receives the pieces and forwards them later over the internet.
The attacker may then unpair the devices and clear local records to hide the activity.
beginner.example: Imagine two people in a cafe who want to swap a photo without using the internet at all. They sit at the same table and send it directly from phone to phone. The picture never travels through a phone company or a website. Bluetooth exfiltration is that shared table. It only works when the two devices are close, but nothing in the middle can watch the photo move.
takeaways: Bluetooth has short range, so proximity is the main problem an attacker must solve.
Pairing records, profile entries and adapter state on the host are your best evidence.
Switch Bluetooth off where it is not needed and review pairings on sensitive machines.

objectives: Explain how this sub-technique differs from the wider other-medium exfiltration technique.
Describe why Bluetooth transfers are slow and require close physical range.
Identify host artefacts such as pairing records, driver activity and adapter state.
Explain why perimeter network monitoring cannot detect this transfer.
Suggest policy steps that reduce Bluetooth exposure on sensitive endpoints.
